q: The physics describing motion, called ____, was discussed in the previous chapter.
e: The physics describing motion, called kinematics, was discussed in the previous chapter. Kinematics names the physics describing motion, called, was discussed in the previous chapter.

q: This chapter is dealt with ____ which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc.
e: This chapter is dealt with dynamics which explains motion in relation to the physical factors that affect motion such as force, momentum, mass etc. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: A fundamental concept in dynamics is ____.
e: A fundamental concept in dynamics is force. Force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: Force is defined precisely by ____.
e: Force is defined precisely by Newton's laws of motion. The physics in this sentence is built around Newton's laws of motion.

q: Force can change the ____ of an object.
e: Force can change the state of motion of an object. The physics in this sentence is built around state of motion.

q: Newton's first law states that: When no ____ acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity.
e: Newton's first law states that: When no net external force acts upon it, a particle at rest will remain at rest and a particle in motion at a constant velocity will continue to move with the same constant velocity. Net external force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: In mathematical form, If ____ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero.
e: In mathematical form, If $F_{net}=0$ then $a=0$, $v=$ constant (or) zero. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: Newton's first law expresses the idea of ____.
e: Newton's first law expresses the idea of inertia. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: ____ is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion.
e: Inertia is the natural property of a body which resists the change of its state of motion. Inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: In fact, the first law is often referred as the ____.
e: In fact, the first law is often referred as the law of inertia. Law of inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the ____ of particle.
c: product of the mass and the acceleration
e: The net external force acting upon a particle is equal to the product of the mass and the acceleration of particle. Product of the mass and the acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest.

q: In mathematical form, ____
e: In mathematical form, $F_{net}=ma$. Net force and acceleration point the same way, and a equals F over m.

q: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the ____.
e: The direction of the acceleration is the same as that of the net force. Net force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is ____ to force.
e: It is equivalent to say that acceleration is directly proportional to force. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Therefore, second law is also called ____.
e: Therefore, second law is also called law of force and acceleration. Law of force and acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is ____ to the force exerted by the first on the second.
c: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
e: Newton's third law of motion states that: Whenever two particles interact, the force exerted by the second on the first is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force exerted by the first on the second. Action and reaction are equal and opposite, and they act on two different bodies.

q: In other words, for every action, there is an ____.
e: In other words, for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. The physics in this sentence is built around equal and opposite reaction.

q: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on ____.
e: Action-reaction pair does not act on a single object but acts on two separate objects. The physics in this sentence is built around two separate objects.

q: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: In SI units, force that is acting on 1 kg mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ is called 1 newton. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called ____.
e: Similarly, in CGS system a force that is acting on 1 g mass to give it an acceleration of $1 \text{ cm s}^{-2}$ is called 1 dyne. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In FPS system the unit of force is ____.
e: In FPS system the unit of force is pound. The unit that belongs with this quantity is pound.

q: The ____ is the unit of mass in British engineering system.
e: The slug is the unit of mass in British engineering system. The unit that belongs with this quantity is slug.

q: Everybody attracts ____ in the universe.
e: Everybody attracts every other body in the universe. The physics in this sentence is built around every other body.

q: The gravitational force between the two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and ____ between them.
c: inversely proportional to the square of the distance
e: The gravitational force between the two bodies is directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. Inversely proportional to the square of the distance here means the path length travelled, with no direction. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: In symbols, ____
e: In symbols, $F \propto \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $F \propto \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$.

q: According to experimental measurements the value of G in MKS system is found to be ____.
e: According to experimental measurements the value of G in MKS system is found to be $6.67 \times 10^{-11} \text{ m}^3 \text{kg}^{-1} \text{s}^{-2}$. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: where G is a ____ which is the same for all bodies in the universe.
e: Where G is a constant which is the same for all bodies in the universe. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause ____.
e: The attractions of the moon and the sun upon water of the earth cause tides. The physics in this sentence is built around tides.

q: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the ____ of the earth.
e: Satellites are kept in their circular orbit by the gravitational attraction of the earth. The physics in this sentence is built around gravitational attraction.

q: Four fundamental forces in nature are all ____.
e: Four fundamental forces in nature are all field forces. The physics in this sentence is built around field forces.

q: They are the gravitational force, weak force, ____ and nuclear force.
e: They are the gravitational force, weak force, electromagnetic force and nuclear force. Electromagnetic force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: ____ is the strongest and the gravitational force is the weakest of these forces.
e: Nuclear force is the strongest and the gravitational force is the weakest of these forces. Nuclear force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: Among the four forces the gravitational and the electromagnetic forces are ____ and the remaining two forces are short-range forces.
e: Among the four forces the gravitational and the electromagnetic forces are long-range forces and the remaining two forces are short-range forces. The physics in this sentence is built around long-range forces.

q: The electromagnetic force acts between ____.
e: The electromagnetic force acts between electric charges. The physics in this sentence is built around electric charges.

q: Weak force acts between ____.
e: Weak force acts between subatomic particles. Subatomic particles here means bits of the medium; the wave can pass energy without carrying them away.

q: Strong nuclear force acts between ____ such as proton, neutron, pion and strange particles.
e: Strong nuclear force acts between elementary particles such as proton, neutron, pion and strange particles. Elementary particles here means bits of the medium; the wave can pass energy without carrying them away.

q: However, unlike gravitational force, these two mechanical forces are not ____.
e: However, unlike gravitational force, these two mechanical forces are not fundamental forces. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows.

q: When a spring is stretched (or) a plastic ruler is bent, the force that causes the spring and the ruler to retain their original form is called ____.
e: When a spring is stretched (or) a plastic ruler is bent, the force that causes the spring and the ruler to retain their original form is called elastic force. Elastic force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: The force that acts to resist the motion of the body is ____.
e: The force that acts to resist the motion of the body is frictional force. Frictional force here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion.

q: The weight of body is the ____ acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling.
e: The weight of body is the force of gravity acting on it which gives its acceleration when it is falling. Force of gravity here means a push or pull that can change a body's state of motion. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The acceleration due to the earth's attraction is called ____ and it is represented by the symbol g.
e: The acceleration due to the earth's attraction is called acceleration due to gravity and it is represented by the symbol g. Acceleration due to gravity here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In FPS system, ____.
e: In FPS system, $g = 32 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $g = 32 \text{ ft s}^{-2}$.

q: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the ____ of the body.
e: The attracting force of the earth acting on a body is defined as the weight of the body. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: The gravitational force acting on the body (or) the weight of the body is found to be ____.
e: The gravitational force acting on the body (or) the weight of the body is found to be $w=mg$. Gravity pulls every mass toward every other mass, weaker as r squared grows. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Weight is a ____ and is directed toward the center of the Earth.
e: Weight is a vector and is directed toward the center of the Earth. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. A vector is not finished until you also say the direction.

q: Mass is the ____ in a body.
e: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body. Quantity of matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: Mass is also a ____.
e: Mass is also a measure of inertia. Measure of inertia here means the natural resistance of a body to a change of motion.

q: The mass of a body defined from this point of view is called ____ while the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass.
e: The mass of a body defined from this point of view is called inertial mass while the mass defined by $m = \frac{W}{g}$ is called gravitational mass. Inertial mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the ____ of the body.
e: Wherever a body may be, there is no change in the value of the mass of the body. Mass here means the quantity of matter, a scalar that does not depend on location.

q: But the ____ of the body can change.
e: But the weight of the body can change. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: Mass is a ____ and always a constant.
e: Mass is a scalar and always a constant. Scalar here means a quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is done once you have the size and the unit.

q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a ____.
e: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration g. Constant acceleration g here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: If the ____ is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall.
e: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall. By definition that quantity is air resistance.

q: Equation of motion under ____ described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall.
e: Equation of motion under constant acceleration described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall. Constant acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In these equations we will use the symbol ____ for displacement s and g for acceleration a.
e: In these equations we will use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration a. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and ____
e: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gh$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gh$.

q: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed ____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed downwards (towards the centre of the earth). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be ____ (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$).
e: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be negative (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the ____, which is written as $p=mv$.
c: product of the mass of the body and its velocity
e: Momentum (p) of a body is defined as the product of the mass of the body and its velocity, which is written as $p=mv$. Product of the mass of the body and its velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Momentum of a body is ____ to its velocity.
e: Momentum of a body is directly proportional to its velocity. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: Momentum is a ____.
e: Momentum is a vector quantity. Vector quantity here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: Direction of momentum is the same as that of ____.
e: Direction of momentum is the same as that of velocity. Velocity here means displacement per time, so direction matters. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Unit of momentum is expressed as the ____.
c: product of mass unit and velocity unit
e: Unit of momentum is expressed as the product of mass unit and velocity unit. Product of mass unit and velocity unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: In MKS system it is ____.
e: In MKS system it is $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.

q: One fundamental law of physics is the ____.
e: One fundamental law of physics is the law of conservation of momentum. Law of conservation of momentum here means mass times velocity, so it is directed. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an ____, the total momentum of the system is constant.
e: This law states that: If there is no net external force acting on an isolated system, the total momentum of the system is constant. Zero net force means constant velocity, including staying at rest. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both ____ objects.
e: The law of conservation of momentum is a general law and is true for both macroscopic and microscopic objects. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.

q: According to law of conservation of momentum, ____ = total momentum after collision.
e: According to law of conservation of momentum, Total momentum before collision = total momentum after collision. Total momentum before collision here means mass times velocity, so it is directed. In an isolated system the total momentum does not change.
